prompt: Why does the lesson install openjdk-21-jdk-headless rather than a package with only the Java runtime?
hint: What has to happen to a test before it runs?

choices.text: The runtime alone cannot open the network connections a test makes
choices.why: A runtime opens connections like any program; boxoffice's clients do it all the time.

choices.text: Only the JDK has the compiler the tests need
choices.why: Right. The runtime only runs finished programs; Maven needs javac to build the tests.

choices.text: headless makes the tests run faster
choices.why: headless only leaves out the libraries for windows; it changes nothing about speed.

choices.text: Maven refuses to install without it
choices.why: apt installs Maven with any Java; the point is what the tests need.

prompt: Match each piece of the Maven setup to what it does.
hint: Section 02 lists three jobs.

pairs.right: the public repository libraries are downloaded from
where downloaded libraries are kept for the next project
where the test code is expected

prompt: A classmate saves the first test as a class called HealthCheck, in the right directory. mvn test prints BUILD SUCCESS. What happened to their test?
hint: Which classes does Surefire look for?

choices.text: It ran and passed, like HealthTest
choices.why: Surefire picks classes by name, and HealthCheck matches none of its patterns.

choices.text: It did not compile, and Maven hid the error
choices.why: It compiles fine; Maven shows compile errors, as section 07 does.

choices.text: It compiled and never ran
choices.why: Right. The name does not end in Test, so Surefire never looked at it, and said nothing.

choices.text: It ran under another name chosen by JUnit
choices.why: JUnit runs what Surefire hands it; nothing renames a class.

prompt: What does <scope>test</scope> on the two dependencies say?
hint: Who uses REST Assured and JUnit?

choices.text: They are downloaded again for every test run
choices.why: They are downloaded once and kept in ~/.m2; scope is about who uses them.

choices.text: They exist only for the tests
choices.why: Right, and in this project the tests are all there is.

choices.text: Their versions are allowed to change between runs
choices.why: The versions are written out whole precisely so that they do not change.

choices.text: They are trial versions that a test may use for free
choices.why: Both are free, open-source libraries; scope says nothing about licences.

prompt: The first mvn test on a new machine fills the screen with "Downloading from central" lines; the libraries are then kept in ~/.___/repository.
hint: A hidden directory in your home, named after Maven.

prompt: Match each part of a REST Assured test to what it holds.
hint: The figure of section 04.

pairs.right: the address, parameters, headers and body
the method and the path, and the sending

right_distractors: the token request, run once per class

prompt: A date filter wrongly returns sh-101 together with sh-103. Which check catches it?
hint: One of the two only asks for "at least".

choices.text: body("shows.id", hasItems("sh-103"))
choices.why: hasItems passes any list that holds sh-103, so the extra show slips through.

choices.text: body("shows.id", contains("sh-103"))
choices.why: Right. contains means exactly this list, in order, and nothing else.

choices.text: statusCode(200)
choices.why: The wrong list still comes with a 200.

choices.text: body("shows.price_cents", everyItem(greaterThan(0)))
choices.why: sh-101 costs 8000 cents, so every price is still above zero.

prompt: Why does ShowsTest never check seats_left of sh-101?
hint: What else in the project touches that show?

choices.text: Because boxoffice does not send seats_left in the list
choices.why: It does; lesson 1's list shows seats_left for every show.

choices.text: Because GPath cannot read a number inside a list
choices.why: GPath reads shows.price_cents in the same class.

choices.text: Because 120 is too big a number for an int
choices.why: An int holds numbers in the billions.

choices.text: Because other tests buy its seats
choices.why: Right. Asserting what another test changes ties the result to the order.

prompt: After hasSize(3) was changed to hasSize(4), on which line of ShowsTest.java did the failure report point?
hint: Look for ShowsTest.theListHasThreeShows followed by a colon.

prompt: In askForAToken, statusCode(200) comes before extract(). What would go wrong if it were left out and the client secret were mistyped?
hint: What is access_token in a 401 answer?

choices.text: Nothing: extract() itself fails on any status that is not 200
choices.why: extract() takes whatever is there; it checks nothing.

choices.text: token would be null and every test would fail with a message about orders
choices.why: Right. The failure would point far from its cause; the check makes it name the cause.

choices.text: The tests would pass, because boxoffice accepts a null token
choices.why: boxoffice answers 401 to a request without a valid bearer token.

choices.text: Maven would refuse to compile the class
choices.why: The compiler knows nothing about status codes; it would compile.

prompt: Put the requests of OrdersTest's flow in the order a run sends them for anOrderCanBeReadBack.
hint: The token is asked for before any test of the class.
items: POST /oauth/token with the client's form fields
POST /v1/orders with the token and a JSON body
extract the location header from the 201
GET that location with the token

prompt: sh-101 starts with 120 seats and each run of OrdersTest buys 2 of them. How many runs in a row succeed before the order is refused with 409, with boxoffice never restarted?
hint: The section says which run is the first refused.

prompt: What does -Dboxoffice.url=http://localhost:8081 change when the order tests run?
hint: Where is BASE read from?

choices.text: It starts a second boxoffice on port 8081
choices.why: Maven starts no server; the second boxoffice was started by hand in a third terminal.

choices.text: It rewrites Api.java with the new address
choices.why: No file changes; the value arrives as a system property while the tests run.

choices.text: The address in the specs, read by System.getProperty
choices.why: Right. Without it, the default http://localhost:8080 is used.

choices.text: Every test class in the project, ShowsTest included, goes to 8081
choices.why: ShowsTest and HealthTest still write their own address and ignore the property.

prompt: Which of these does the spec returned by Api.as("ci-tests", "ci-secret") carry?
hint: Read the RequestSpecBuilder at the end of the method.

choices.text: The address of boxoffice
choices.why: Right, through addRequestSpecification(ANYONE).

choices.text: A bearer token for ci-tests
choices.why: Right: setAuth(oauth2(token)).

choices.text: The JSON content type
choices.why: Right: setContentType(ContentType.JSON).

choices.text: The expected status code 201
choices.why: A request spec describes requests; checks on responses are what PROBLEM, a response spec, holds.

prompt: noTokenIs401AndSaysWhy no longer sends a body and still gets 401. What does that show about boxoffice?
hint: Which question does boxoffice ask first?

choices.text: That it ignores the body of every POST, whatever the token
choices.why: It reads the body once the token is valid; a missing show_id gives a 422.

choices.text: That it checks who is asking before reading what was sent
choices.why: Right. A server that parsed an anonymous body first would do work, and could leak detail, for nobody.

choices.text: That a missing body counts as a missing token
choices.why: The www-authenticate header says "no bearer token", which is about the header.

choices.text: That the PROBLEM response spec added the 401 status itself
choices.why: A response spec only checks; the 401 is what boxoffice sent.

prompt: Without the Surefire block, mvn test printed Tests run: 0 and BUILD SUCCESS, with HeadTest still in the project. Why did it not fail?
hint: Which Surefire ran?

choices.text: Maven's default Surefire predates JUnit Jupiter and found no test to run
choices.why: Right. Zero tests ran, so zero failed, and the build was green.

choices.text: boxoffice was stopped, so the tests were skipped
choices.why: boxoffice was running; a stopped server gives errors, not skipped tests.

choices.text: -q hides failures
choices.why: -q hides progress; a failure is printed in full, as section 07 shows.

choices.text: The compiler skipped the test classes
choices.why: The tests compiled; the compile failure only came when the compiler block went too.

prompt: The pipeline must stop a merge when HeadTest fails. What does it read from mvn test?
hint: The last command of section 07's first run.

choices.text: The word FAILURE in the output
choices.why: Text changes with versions and languages; a pipeline reads something steadier.

choices.text: The colour of the output
choices.why: The colour is removed when output is not a terminal, and a CI log may have none.

choices.text: The exit code, 1
choices.why: Right, as with Newman in lesson 6.

choices.text: The .txt report of each class
choices.why: Those are for people; a CI server's test list comes from the XML, and the stop from the exit code.

prompt: Match each thing in the failing run to what it tells you.
hint: Section 07 reads it in four blocks.

pairs.right: what was sent, logged because a check failed
which check failed and what came back
the line of your own code to open
how many tests ran, and how many failed

right_distractors: how long boxoffice took to start

prompt: A pipeline runs mvn -q test -Dboxoffice.url=https://staging.example against a staging server. ShowsTest passes there although staging's list is broken. What is the likeliest reason?
hint: Which classes read the property?

choices.text: -q hid ShowsTest's failures
choices.why: -q never hides a failure; it hides progress.

choices.text: It still sends every request to localhost:8080
choices.why: Right. Only the classes built on Api.BASE follow the property; ShowsTest tested whatever answered on the build machine.

choices.text: Staging answers HTTPS, which REST Assured does not check
choices.why: REST Assured speaks HTTPS; the problem is where the requests went.

choices.text: Surefire ran ShowsTest before the property was read
choices.why: The property is there from the start of the test JVM; order is not the issue.

prompt: You want a test that a cancelled order cannot be read as confirmed. Which flow is right?
hint: The test has to create what it checks.

choices.text: GET /v1/orders/ord-1001 and expect status cancelled
choices.why: ord-1001 may not exist, may belong to another run, and nothing cancelled it.

choices.text: DELETE the location that anOrderCanBeReadBack created, from another test
choices.why: That ties the new test to another test's state and order, which JUnit does not promise.

choices.text: POST an order, DELETE its location (204), then GET it: cancelled
choices.why: Right. The test makes its own order, so it depends on nothing else.

choices.text: DELETE /v1/orders and expect every order to be cancelled
choices.why: boxoffice answers only POST on /v1/orders; DELETE there is a 405.

prompt: A colleague changes HeadTest to expect 405 "so the build is green". What is wrong with that?
hint: What is a test for?

choices.text: Nothing, as long as the comment at the top is updated
choices.why: The comment would then describe the defect as the expected behaviour.

choices.text: 405 is not a status REST Assured can check
choices.why: statusCode takes any number; 405 is checkable.

choices.text: The test would then fail when run with -q
choices.why: -q changes the printing, not the verdict.

choices.text: The test would assert the defect, and fail on the day the server is fixed
choices.why: Right. A red test that names a known defect is information; turning it green by expecting the defect hides it.
